full_judgment:
"115 Revision (1) The High Court Division may, on the application of any party aggrieved, call for the record of any suit or proceeding in which a decree or an order has been passed by a Court of District Judge or Additional District Judge or a decree has been passed by a Court of Joint District Judge, Senior Assistant Judge or Assistant Judge from which no appeal lies; and if such Court appears to have committed any error of law resulting in an error in such decree or order occasioning failure of justice, the High Court Division may, revise such decree or order and, make such order in the suit or proceeding as it thinks fit. 

 Section 21(1)Save as aforesaid, an appeal from a decree or order of a Joint District Judge shall lie- 

 (a) to the District Judge where the value of the original suit in which or in any proceeding arising out of which the decree or order was made did not exceed five lac Taka, and 

 (2) Save as aforesaid and appeal from a decree or order of Senior Assistant Judge or Assistant Judge shall lie to the District Judge. 

 12. Section 19 of the Civil Courts Act provides for the pecuniary jurisdiction of Senior Assistant Judge and Assistant Judge in respect of suit. Sub-section 2 of section 21 indicates that an appeal shall lie to the District Judge against a decree or order passed by the Senior Assistant Judge or Assistant Judge. Order as employed in sub-section (2) implies appealable order as contemplated under Order XLIII, rule (1) of the Code of Civil Procedure or any order passed in any proceeding like pre-emption proceeding. Suits or proceedings of which the vahie exceeds four lac Taka will lie to the Joint District Judge having unlimited pecuniary jurisdiction. But, according to the provision of sub-section (1) of section 21 appeal from a decree or order passed by the Joint District Judge will lie to the District Judge in which the value of the original suit or proceeding did not exceed Taka five lac. Therefore, in a suit filed before the Joint District Judge the value of which does not exceed five lac Taka, if a decree or order, as the case may be is passed appeal will lie to the District Judge. As per Clause (b) of sub-section (1) of section 21 appeal will lie to the High Court Division in any other cases i.e. when the value does exceed Taka 5 lac. 

 "22(1) A District Judge may transfer to any Joint District Judge under his Administrative Control any appeals pending before him from the decree or orders of Assistant Judges.
